name: Crispy Miso-Caramel Oven-Fried Chicken Wings

ingredients.name: chicken wings, cut into drumettes and flats, divided

instructions.primary_message: For the Wings: Line a rimmed baking sheet with aluminum foil and set a wire rack inside. Carefully dry chicken wings with paper towels. In a large bowl, combine 0.45 kg wings with 1 teaspoon baking powder and 1 teaspoon salt, and toss until thoroughly and evenly coated. Place on rack, leaving a slight space between each wing. Repeat with remaining wings, baking powder, and salt.
Refrigerate baking sheet with wings, uncovered, at least 8 hours and up to 24 hours.

When ready to cook, adjust oven rack to upper-middle position and preheat oven to 230°C (450°F). Cook chicken wings for 20 minutes. Flip wings and continue to cook until crisp and golden brown, 15 to 30 minutes longer, flipping a few more times towards the end.

For the Miso-Caramel Glaze: Meanwhile, in a medium saucepan, combine brown sugar, miso, fish sauce, rice vinegar, and garlic, and bring to a simmer over medium heat. Stir until sugar dissolves and simmer until mixture thickens to a glaze-like consistency that coats the back of a spoon, 5 to 10 minutes. Remove from heat and set aside.
Transfer wings to a large bowl and toss with prepared sauce until coated evenly. Sprinkle with sesame seeds and toss to coat. Serve wings immediately.

schema_metadata.keywords: Crispy Miso-Caramel Oven-Fried Chicken Wings, chicken wings recipe, oven-baked chicken wings, oven-fried chicken wings

description: These oven-baked chicken wings are shatteringly crisp and coated in a sticky miso-caramel glaze that balances savoriness with just enough sweetness.
notes:
Total time, including resting: 8 hr 55 min.

Optional or for serving: 1 to 2 tablespoons toasted sesame seeds for sprinkling

Notes: We prefer to buy whole chicken wings and butcher them ourselves, but you can also use presplit wings.

Make-ahead and storage: Wings are best served immediately, but can be safely stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days.
author: Leah Colins
